title: A Festival with an Extra Entrance
title_ja: もう一つの入口を設けた祭り
fact_notes: 人物・町・行事・数値や結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: Every autumn, volunteers in a small town decorated a narrow street for a traditional evening festival.
sentences.ja: 毎年秋、小さな町のボランティアは伝統的な夜祭りのため狭い通りを飾りつけた。

sentences.en: The main entrance was especially popular because visitors could see a large display of lanterns as they arrived.
sentences.ja: 正面入口は到着時に大きなちょうちんの飾りを見られるため特に人気があった。

sentences.en: However, the entrance required people to take several steps down into the street before reaching the festival area.
sentences.ja: しかし祭りの会場に着く前に、その入口では階段を数段下りる必要があった。

sentences.en: Some visitors had difficulty entering, and others decided not to attend the festival at all.
sentences.ja: 入るのに苦労する来場者もいれば、祭りへの参加を諦める人もいた。

sentences.en: A young volunteer suggested creating a second entrance from a nearby public square where the ground was level.
sentences.ja: 若いボランティアは地面が平らな近くの広場から第二の入口を作ることを提案した。

sentences.en: Several older organizers worried that visitors using the new entrance would miss an important part of the traditional experience.
sentences.ja: 年長の主催者の数人は新入口を利用する人が伝統的な体験の重要な一部を逃すのではと心配した。

sentences.en: Rather than dismissing their concern, the volunteer asked them which elements of the entrance they considered particularly meaningful.
sentences.ja: 懸念を退ける代わりに、入口のどの要素を特に意義深いと考えるか尋ねた。

sentences.en: They explained that passing beneath the lanterns marked the beginning of a special evening for the whole community.
sentences.ja: ちょうちんの下を通ることが地域全体にとって特別な夜の始まりを示すと説明した。

sentences.en: The organizers therefore explored ways to create a similar welcome at the second entrance without copying every physical detail.
sentences.ja: そこで主催者は物理的な細部をすべて再現せずに第二入口でも同様の歓迎を作る方法を検討した。

sentences.en: Local artists designed a smaller display of lanterns and placed it where visitors could enjoy it from different heights.
sentences.ja: 地元の芸術家は小さなちょうちん飾りを設計し、異なる高さから楽しめる場所に置いた。

sentences.en: Volunteers tested the new route together with residents who used wheelchairs or needed more space to walk comfortably.
sentences.ja: 車椅子利用者や快適に歩くため広い空間が必要な住民と一緒に新ルートを試した。

sentences.en: They made several adjustments after listening to suggestions about the position of signs and the width of the path.
sentences.ja: 標識の位置や道幅についての提案を聞き、いくつかの修正をした。

sentences.en: On the evening of the festival, both entrances offered visitors an opportunity to pass through a display of lights.
sentences.ja: 祭りの夜には両方の入口で来場者が光の飾りを通り抜ける機会を得られた。

sentences.en: The organizers explained the two routes on their invitations so that families could choose before leaving home.
sentences.ja: 家を出る前に家族が選べるよう、招待案内に二つのルートを説明した。

sentences.en: After the festival, they collected comments rather than assume that the new design had solved every remaining access problem.
sentences.ja: 祭りの後、新デザインが残るすべてのアクセス問題を解決したと決めつけず、意見を集めた。

sentences.en: Several residents suggested further improvements that the organizers planned to consider for the following year.
sentences.ja: 住民数人がさらなる改善を提案し、主催者は翌年に向けて検討することにした。

sentences.en: The experience showed the volunteers that preserving a tradition need not mean keeping every feature of an event unchanged.
sentences.ja: 体験から、伝統を守るとは行事の特徴をすべて変えずにおくこととは限らないと分かった。

sentences.en: Understanding the purpose of a familiar custom can reveal opportunities to adapt it without losing its central meaning.
sentences.ja: なじみのある習慣の目的を理解すれば、中心的な意味を失わず変える機会が見えてくる。

sentences.en: Such changes are more likely to be useful when the people affected by them help shape the decisions.
sentences.ja: そうした変更の影響を受ける人が決定に関わると、より役立つ可能性がある。

sentences.en: For these organizers, the festival became an opportunity to share their heritage rather than a test of who could enter.
sentences.ja: 主催者にとって祭りは誰が入れるかを試す場ではなく、文化遺産を共有する機会になった。

questions.prompt: Why was the main entrance popular?
options: It had no stairs at all.
Tickets were sold there at a lower price.
Visitors could see a large lantern display.
The festival always ended at that point.
questions.explanation_ja: 大きなちょうちん飾りが見られた。

questions.prompt: What made entry difficult for some visitors?
options: They needed to go down several steps.
All visitors needed to carry lanterns.
The street was closed before sunset.
The festival required an expensive ticket.
questions.explanation_ja: 階段を数段下りる必要があった。

questions.prompt: What did the young volunteer propose?
options: Removing every lantern from the festival.
Moving the event to a distant town.
Ending the tradition of evening celebrations.
A second entrance from a level public square.
questions.explanation_ja: 平らな広場から第二入口を提案。

questions.prompt: Why were some organizers concerned about the proposal?
options: They believed nobody used the original entrance.
They feared losing a meaningful part of the welcoming experience.
They wanted the festival to become an indoor event.
They were unable to find the public square.
questions.explanation_ja: 伝統的な歓迎の体験を失うと心配。

questions.prompt: How did artists recreate the welcome?
options: They played a recorded speech at the old entrance.
They built stairs in the new route.
They designed another lantern display.
They gave every guest an identical lantern.
questions.explanation_ja: 第二のちょうちん飾りを作った。

questions.prompt: Who helped test the new route?
options: Residents with different mobility needs.
Only the oldest festival organizers.
Visitors who had never entered the town.
A group of school examination candidates.
questions.explanation_ja: 車椅子利用者など住民の協力を得た。

options: Only inside the main entrance.
On festival invitations.
On a closed private notebook.
After all visitors had left the festival.
questions.explanation_ja: 招待案内にルートを紹介した。

questions.prompt: Why did organizers collect comments afterward?
options: They knew every possible problem had been solved.
They intended to cancel the festival immediately.
They wanted to remove both entrances.
They recognized that access problems might remain.
questions.explanation_ja: まだ改善が必要な可能性があった。

options: Cultural traditions passed down over time.
A newly purchased vehicle.
A temporary path under construction.
A personal examination result.
questions.explanation_ja: 受け継がれる文化や伝統。

options: Traditional events should never be changed in any way.
New entrances necessarily destroy all cultural meanings.
Traditions can be adapted to include more people while preserving their purpose.
Accessibility should be planned without consulting users.
questions.explanation_ja: 伝統の意味と参加しやすさを両立できる。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 形式そのものではなく歓迎の意味を再現する。
